statusModelDecision.chosen: REUSE the existing NodeSupersessionStatus literal "KNOWN_SUPERSEDED" for whole-document supersession too - do NOT add a new NodeSupersessionStatus union member.
statusModelDecision.why: 02-consumer-inventory.json found zero D-classification (unsafe-bypass) consumers and two exhaustive Record<NodeSupersessionStatus, number> maps (orchestrator.ts, discovery/pass-d-reconcile.ts) that every consumer's worst-first severity ranking already depends on. Every real consumer already treats KNOWN_SUPERSEDED as the fail-closed, non-current, most-severe signal. Reusing it means the entire consumer graph inherits correct behavior with zero downstream code changes and zero risk of a future switch/if-chain silently falling through a literal it doesn't recognize yet (a real risk a brand-new status value would introduce, since TypeScript's structural typing does not force every existing conditional to be revisited).
statusModelDecision.whyIsThisTheSmallestAdditive: The mission's own Section 8 says 'prefer reusing existing status vocabulary; if needed, add smallest additive status.' Reuse is possible here because KNOWN_SUPERSEDED's own existing meaning ('this physical occurrence's text no longer governs') is a strict superset that already covers 'this physical occurrence's ENTIRE CONTAINING DOCUMENT no longer governs' - the provenance distinction (why) is preserved via a new field on the record, not the status enum, exactly mirroring how a KNOWN_SUPERSEDED record already varies in provenance depending on which effect/document caused it.

changes: NodeSupersessionRecord gains two new REQUIRED fields (every existing construction site - the one pre-existing call in buildNodeSupersessionIndex's own per-provision loop - is updated in the same commit, so no optional/undefined migration hazard): `supersessionKind: "PROVISION_LEVEL" | "DOCUMENT_LEVEL"` and `supersedingOperativeDocumentId: string | null` (populated only for DOCUMENT_LEVEL; null for PROVISION_LEVEL).

NodeSupersessionIndex gains one new field: `documentLevelSupersededDocuments: Map<string, NodeSupersessionRecord>` - keyed by documentId (NOT nodeId, since a whole-document verdict applies uniformly to every node in that document without needing to enumerate them - directly satisfies the mission's 'do not require enumerating every physical node' concern).
typeChanges_typesTs.whyNotNodeIdKeyed: The existing supersededByNodeId map is necessarily nodeId-keyed because provision-level supersession is inherently per-node (only the specific section/definition an amendment targeted is superseded). Whole-document supersession applies uniformly to EVERY node in a historical predecessor document - keying by documentId avoids ever needing to know the full set of nodeIds a document contains, and lets getNodeSupersessionStatus answer correctly for a node it has never seen before, exactly like the existing coveredDocumentIds set already does for the CURRENT_OPERATIVE default.

logicChanges_operativeStateTs.buildNodeSupersessionIndex: After the existing per-provision loop (unchanged), for each `{baseDocumentId, state}` entry: if `state.operativeDocument?.status === "RESOLVED"` AND `baseDocumentId !== state.operativeDocument.operativeDocumentId` AND `state.operativeDocument.predecessorDocumentIds.includes(baseDocumentId)`, look up the DIRECT successor edge for baseDocumentId in `state.operativeDocument.relationshipChain` (the edge where `restatesDocumentId === baseDocumentId`) for its own effectId/successor documentId/effectiveDate provenance, and register a DOCUMENT_LEVEL record in the new `documentLevelSupersededDocuments` map (first-writer-wins across entries, mirroring the existing per-node map's own defensive convention).
logicChanges_operativeStateTs.getNodeSupersessionStatus: New RULE 1 check inserted immediately after the existing 'no nodeId supplied' fail-closed branch and BEFORE the existing per-node supersededByNodeId lookup: if `index.documentLevelSupersededDocuments.has(documentId)`, return KNOWN_SUPERSEDED with that record (nodeId field filled in with the actual queried nodeId - the stored template has no real nodeId of its own since it applies to the whole document), reason explicitly naming the resolved operative document. This composes as the mission's RULE 1 ('RESOLVED whole-document supersession wins') taking priority over RULE 2 (existing per-node record) - both would return the identical KNOWN_SUPERSEDED status/behavior for any downstream consumer regardless of which fires first, so the ordering is a provenance-quality choice (document-level reason is more informative when both could apply), not a behavioral one.
logicChanges_operativeStateTs.EMPTY_SUPERSESSION_INDEX: Updated to include `documentLevelSupersededDocuments: new Map()` - the fail-closed default already returns UNKNOWN for everything via the pre-existing coveredDocumentIds check, so this addition is inert for EMPTY_SUPERSESSION_INDEX, exactly as intended.

rule5_ordinaryAmendmentSafety.requirement: An ordinary amendment (V1 -> First Amendment, no whole-document restatement) must NOT imply V1 is historical as a whole.
rule5_ordinaryAmendmentSafety.howThisDesignGuaranteesIt: computeOperativeDocument (chain.ts, UNCHANGED by this session) only ever produces status RESOLVED when restatementEffects.length > 0 - i.e. at least one real RESTATE_AGREEMENT-operation effect exists. An ordinary amendment's own effects use REPLACE_TEXT/MODIFY_THRESHOLD/ADD_EXCEPTION/etc - never RESTATE_AGREEMENT - so computeOperativeDocument returns NOT_APPLICABLE for that instrument, `state.operativeDocument.status` is NOT "RESOLVED", and the new RULE 1 branch in getNodeSupersessionStatus never fires. V1's own untouched sections fall through to the pre-existing RULE 3 default (CURRENT_OPERATIVE), and V1's own amended sections continue to be governed by the pre-existing, unmodified per-provision logic (RULE 2) exactly as before. This is a structural guarantee (falls out of computeOperativeDocument's own pre-existing gating on RESTATE_AGREEMENT effects), not a special case this session had to add.

rule6_neverGuessUncertainty.requirement: REVIEW_REQUIRED/ambiguous/forked/cyclic/incomplete/unresolved whole-document state must never be converted into supersession.
rule6_neverGuessUncertainty.howThisDesignGuaranteesIt: The new RULE 1 branch gates strictly on `state.operativeDocument?.status === "RESOLVED"` - every other status value (REVIEW_REQUIRED for forks/cycles/unresolved-target restatement effects per chain.ts's own existing safe-failure branches, or NOT_APPLICABLE) leaves documentLevelSupersededDocuments untouched for that entry, so getNodeSupersessionStatus falls through to its pre-existing RULE 2/3/4 behavior exactly as before this session. No new uncertainty-to-certainty conversion is introduced anywhere in this design.

provenanceRequirement.neverDeletePredecessorNodes: This design touches ONLY the trust/status layer (buildNodeSupersessionIndex/getNodeSupersessionStatus's own return values) - it introduces no code path that deletes, mutates, or hides any StructuralNode, StructuralIndex entry, or raw document text anywhere. getRawNodeText (semantic/tools.ts) and every other raw-text accessor remain fully able to retrieve a DOCUMENT_LEVEL-superseded node's own text - only its TRUST metadata (supersessionStatus) changes.
provenanceRequirement.retrievableNotEqualCurrent: Verified by design: nodeSupersession.status is consulted only by trust-gating logic (evidenceCurrent booleans, determineStatus's REVIEW_REQUIRED routing) - never by any node lookup/retrieval function itself. A caller that explicitly wants historical text (e.g. getPriorVersion/getRelatedAmendments per semantic/tools.ts's own existing tool descriptions) is unaffected.

explicitlyRejectedAlternative.alternative: Add a new NodeSupersessionStatus literal, e.g. "SUPERSEDED_BY_DOCUMENT_VERSION".
explicitlyRejectedAlternative.whyRejected: Would require updating the two exhaustive Record<NodeSupersessionStatus, number> severity maps (orchestrator.ts, pass-d-reconcile.ts) merely to keep them compiling, for zero behavioral benefit over reusing KNOWN_SUPERSEDED (both literals mean exactly the same thing to every real consumer: 'do not trust this as current'). It would also silently risk a FUTURE consumer that explicitly enumerates `status === "KNOWN_SUPERSEDED"` as its only non-CURRENT_OPERATIVE branch (a pattern already used in verify.ts's determineStatus and semantic/tools.ts's legacySupersessionDisplay) failing to recognize the new literal as equally untrustworthy - a real, avoidable regression risk the reuse-based design eliminates entirely.
